item.description: Depletion interactions play a critical role in colloidal stability, yet their behavior in ligand-coated, anisotropic nanocrystals remains poorly understood due to the limitations of hard-particle assumptions at soft interfaces. In two-dimensional (2D) nanoplatelets (NPLs), atomically flat surfaces amplify excluded-volume overlap, leading to strong depletion-driven aggregation in multicomponent environments. Here, we show that the nanoscale configuration of the ligand shell serves as a key...

item.title: A grounded theory of compassionate care among clinical nurses
item.description: BackgroundCompassionate care is a core ethical obligation in nursing, yet the processes through which nurses enact and sustain it remain insufficiently theorized. Existing grounded theory models have not examined an East Asian care context in which nursing staff may assume both clinical and daily living care.Research question/aim/objectivesHow do clinical nurses experience, construct, and sustain compassionate care, and what ethical challenges shape this process?Research designA grounded theory...

item.title: Cerebral Hemodynamic Changes in Older Adults With Cognitive Complaints According to the Presence of Peripheral Artery Disease
item.description: CONCLUSION: These findings identify PAD as a condition associated with progressive MCA MFV elevation in the context of preserved cognition, implying that subclinical cerebrovascular changes are detectable by TCD before overt clinical worsening. Future research involving larger cohorts and extended follow-up is required to determine whether such hemodynamic changes forecast eventual cognitive deterioration.

item.title: Reliability of MRI-based grading using Yoon's classification for labral tears in hip dysplasia
item.description: Labral tears in hip dysplasia arise from structural instability and excessive shear forces. Yoon's classification system, based on arthroscopic findings, was developed to reflect the natural course of labral tears in hip dysplasia and guide surgical decision-making. However, its reliability when applied to MRI-based grading remains unclear. We retrospectively included 105 hips from 88 patients with hip dysplasia, including borderline hip dysplasia, who underwent arthroscopic labral repair...

item.title: Pain mediates the association between psychological distress and increases in inflammation in middle-aged and older rural adults: A longitudinal cohort study
item.description: Rural populations are under-represented in empirical studies testing associations between psychological distress, pain, and inflammation, despite known health disparities between rural and urban areas. This study examined associations between psychological distress symptoms and change in the inflammatory marker C-reactive protein (CRP), whether pain and functional limitations accounted for this association, and whether observed patterns varied among urban or rural adults. Participants were...

item.title: Validation of a Revised V-Slope Algorithm for Automated First Ventilatory Threshold Detection in Healthy Adults
item.description: CONCLUSION: The revised V-slope algorithm demonstrated strong group-level agreement with visual assessment for VT1 determination, supporting the reliability and practical applicability for large-scale research applications in healthy adults. However, given the observed individual-level variability, caution is warranted when applying automated VT1 values to guide exercise prescription for individual patients without expert review.

item.title: Haemophagocytic Lymphohistiocytosis Triggered by Visceral Leishmaniasis Masquerading as Epstein-Barr Virus (EBV)-Associated Haemophagocytic Lymphohistiocytosis in Rheumatoid Arthritis: A Case Report and Literature Review
item.description: Haemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis (HLH) is a life-threatening hyperinflammatory syndrome caused by uncontrolled immune activation. In adults, it is usually secondary to an underlying condition, such as infection, malignancy, or autoimmune disease. Identifying this trigger is essential, as treatment depends on the cause. Visceral leishmaniasis (VL) is a systemic parasitic infection that may mimic or trigger HLH, particularly in immunosuppressed patients. We report a 59-year-old man with...

item.title: Development and Clinical Evaluation of an Anterior Chamber Angle-Based Lens Sizing Method for Implantable Collamer Lens Surgery
item.description: CONCLUSION: An ICL sizing approach incorporating a preoperative angle-based threshold formula (the CEC method) was associated with a lower frequency of postoperative narrow-angle classification and warrants further prospective validation.

item.title: Rapidly growing pulmonary inflammatory myofibroblastic tumor: a case report
item.description: CONCLUSION: IMT rarely presents with rapid growth and should be considered in the differential diagnosis of tumors with a doubling time <20 days.

item.title: A Meibomian Gland Concretion Presenting as a Palpable Eyelid Mass: A Rare Case Report
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: This case demonstrates a rare presentation of multiple interconnected concretions forming a clinically visible and palpable eyelid-margin mass. The combination of the clinical and operative findings, macroscopic appearance, and histopathological characteristics supported a diagnosis of meibomian gland concretion, although glandular or ductal tissue was not identified in the examined fragments.

item.title: A rare case of dysplasia epiphysealis hemimelica in a hip joint treated by arthroscopic tumour resection: a case report
item.description: We report a rare case of dysplasia epiphysealis hemimelica (DEH) in a hip joint treated by arthroscopic tumour resection. A 12-year-old male developed difficulty walking due to progressive right hip pain that had persisted for 3 months. Radiography revealed subluxation of the right hip, and magnetic resonance imaging revealed a prominent elevated lesion on the acetabular roof. DEH of the hip was suspected; the tumour was resected via arthroscopy, which resolved the hip pain and subluxation. This...

item.title: Diagnostic variability of mental disorders in adolescence: A longitudinal study across transition boundary age
item.description: CONCLUSION: This study highlights the diagnostic stability of most psychiatric conditions during the transition from CAMHS to AMHS. Given the complexity of adolescent mental health, accurate and continuous assessment is crucial. Understanding the evolving nature of psychiatric symptoms during adolescence will improve diagnostic accuracy and inform better interventions, fostering long-term mental health outcomes.

item.title: Incidence and risk factors for postoperative posterior column fractures following periacetabular osteotomy
item.description: Periacetabular osteotomy (PAO) is a widely used surgical technique for symptomatic developmental dysplasia of the hip (DDH). However, the incidence of posterior column fractures after PAO and the risk factors are not adequately investigated. Identification rates have been improved by using oblique radiographs, but few reports have examined the incidence of posterior column fractures using early postoperative computed tomography (CT) scans. This study aimed to investigate the incidence and risk...

item.title: Wood type influences tree responses to recurring hot and dry summer tree water deficits across European forests
item.description: Increasingly frequent summer droughts are intensifying stem dehydration across European forests, constraining tree growth and resilience. Even mild water-related stress can inhibit tree growth, although its impact is species-specific. Tree water deficit (TWD), a measure deduced from radial stem contraction during drought, reflects stem water status and can be used as a proxy for the physiological drought stress experienced by trees. Using high-resolution dendrometer measurements representing 29...

item.title: The hearing healthcare workforce: insights into density, distribution and opportunities for capacity-development
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: These findings highlight critical disparities and emphasise the need for targeted workforce planning and sustainable training programs to improve global hearing care.

item.title: Ambivalent return: Older adults' homecoming after wartime displacement
item.description: OBJECTIVES: Little is known about how older adults experience their return home after wartime displacement, particularly when home and community are altered or remain insecure. This longitudinal qualitative study examined continuity and change across the displacement-return transition.

item.title: Evaluation of Three Automated Pretreatment Workstations for Free Silica Determination
item.description: CONCLUSION: All three workstations are safe, reliable alternatives to manual PPA digestion and agreed with the manual method on field samples.

item.title: Immunosuppressant-refractory Multifaceted Immune Dysregulations for Systemic Lupus Erythematosus
item.description: While the systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE), a severe autoimmune disease, is known to relapse frequently after treatment, none of the previous single-cell studies have examined the immune dynamics and their potential contribution to this relapse in the real clinical setting. To address this issue, here we employed single-cell multi-omics profiling to delineate immune repertoire dynamics during the immunosuppressant-based standard of care. Further analysis showed that the canonical therapy fails...

item.title: Excessive Feed Sorting Is Associated With Altered Plasma Metabolism and Distinct Fermentation Responses of Pooled Rumen Microbiota in Dairy Cows
item.description: Feed sorting behaviour in dairy cows alters dietary structure and has been associated with rumen dysfunction, but its systemic metabolic consequences and microbial acidogenic potential remain unclear. This study combined in vivo and in vitro approaches to investigate associations between feed sorting behaviour, host metabolism, and rumen microbial fermentation. Twenty-four mid-lactation Holstein cows were monitored for 28 days, from which 12 cows representing extreme feed-sorting phenotypes were...

item.title: Perfusion quality does not necessarily predict ultrastructural preservation after hyperosmotic brain perfusion
item.description: Perfusion fixation is widely used in neuroscience to prepare mammalian brain tissue for histological and ultrastructural analysis. Perfusion protocols are commonly assessed using macroscopic indicators such as gross appearance and neuroimaging, which assess the extent to which perfusate has been distributed throughout the brain. There is a critical need to determine to what extent these metrics can accurately predict high-quality ultrastructural preservation, particularly as new perfusion...

item.title: How Community Pharmacists Use Their Know-Who When Dispensing Medicines: A Qualitative Study
item.description: CONCLUSION: Community pharmacists integrate 'Know-Who' with theoretical and practical knowledge to make contextually informed, patient-centered decisions. This relational dimension enables them to manage uncertainty, optimise communication, and foster effective interprofessional collaboration. These findings underscore the importance of incorporating relational and contextual knowledge into pharmacy education and training, and suggest that acknowledging the role of 'Know-Who' could enhance both...

item.title: Secondhand smoke exposure and fetal loss in nonsmoking pregnant women: a meta-analysis
item.description: CONCLUSION: This study provided compelling evidence that secondhand smoke exposure during pregnancy increased the risk of fetal loss, emphasizing the need for avoidance.

item.title: Left Atrial Appendage Closure Versus Oral Anticoagulation for Prevention of Stroke or Systemic Embolism in Patients With Atrial Fibrillation: An Updated Meta-Analysis of 7004 Patients Across Six Randomized Trials
item.description: CONCLUSION: LAAC demonstrates comparable risks of SSE and major bleeding to OACs, but is associated with a higher risk of ischemic SSE and reduced non-procedural bleeding, supporting its use in selected patients at high risk for long-term bleeding while emphasizing individualized shared decision-making.

item.title: Regional lean mass, bone mineral measures, and estimated leg press 1-RM in resistance-trained males
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: In resistance-trained males, regional DXA lean mass and bone measures appear to form a phenotype that is strongly influenced by body size. Associations from models adjusted for age and height should therefore be interpreted alongside the size conditioned analyzes. The association between pelvis BMC and estimated leg press 1-RM is best viewed as an exploratory conditional finding within this broader phenotype, rather than evidence of a distinct skeletal contribution to strength.

item.description: High-capacity Li-rich Mn-based oxide cathodes exhibit exceptional specific capacity density; however, their utilization encounters challenges pertaining to sluggish Li^(+) ion transport kinetics and severe interfacial issues in high-voltage lithium-ion batteries, especially under the working condition of fast charging. Here, a protective biphasic shell layer coupled with B/Al co-doping in the near-surface bulk phase region is designed on Li(1.2)Mn(0.54)Ni(0.13)Co(0.13)O(2) cathode by means of...

item.title: Tough Glassy Hydrogels of High Water Content via Polymerization-Induced Hydrogen Bonding and Phase Separation of Block Copolymers
item.description: Tough glassy hydrogels that rely on robust noncovalent interactions of copolymers typically suffer from low water content, because random monomer sequences hinder the formation of ordered intermolecular associations and well-organized network architectures. Here, we report tough poly(methacrylic acid)-block-poly(methacrylamide) (PMAAc-b-PMAAm) hydrogels with high water content, fabricated via the reversible addition-fragmentation chain transfer (RAFT) polymerization that results in hydrogen...

item.description: Large birefringence is a key parameter for nonlinear optical (NLO) and birefringent crystals, as it is critical for extending the phase-matching wavelength of NLO crystals and optimizing the light-splitting performance of birefringent crystals. item.title: Sleep trajectories in pregnancy: associations with trauma exposure, PTSD, and postpartum depression
item.description: Sleep during the perinatal period is often highly disrupted due to maternal biopsychosocial changes that accompany pregnancy. Poor sleep quality is a symptom of PTSD, while insomnia often emerges after a traumatic event and commonly co-occurs with PTSD. Trauma exposure as well as insomnia have been linked to increased risk for postpartum depression (PPD). The current study examined sleep trajectories across pregnancy and into the postpartum period, the impact of trauma exposure and PTSD on these...

item.title: Social Media and HPV Vaccine Hesitancy: How Misinformation Affects Latino Parents
item.description: Human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccine coverage in the United States remains suboptimal, with Latino communities facing disproportionately lower rates and a higher burden of HPV-associated cancers. Health misinformation and disinformation (M&D) on social media represents a barrier to HPV vaccine uptake, yet little empirical evidence exists on how such content shapes vaccine decision-making. We conducted a cross-sectional study of 98 Latino parents drawn from two randomized, community-based...

item.description: ObjectiveTo evaluate an incident-level framework for predicting whether a newly reported wildfire would reach at least 10 ha, emphasizing temporal validation, statistical benchmarking, and transparent optimizer assessment using only information available at or near incident registration.MethodsThis retrospective modelling study integrated 1,901 operational wildfire records documented by the Mersin Regional Directorate of Forestry during 2004-2025 with event-day meteorology and Canadian Fire...

item.title: Sicker at all ages? Two decades of changing disease histories and mortality in the United States
item.description: CONCLUSION: Stagnating US mortality reflects both the growing prevalence of high-morbidity profiles and worsening or stagnating survival within them, highlighting the limited reach of prevention and disease-management efforts.

item.title: Maternal smoking and risk of childhood cancer: a report from the Childhood Cancer and Leukemia International Consortium
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: This analysis supports previous findings that there is little evidence of an effect of maternal prenatal smoking on childhood cancer risk, with few potential exceptions. However, due to numerous other detrimental effects, public health efforts should continue to further reduce its prevalence.

item.description: Although the Golgi apparatus undergoes extensive disassembly during mitosis to ensure its equitable partitioning into two daughter cells, the extreme asymmetry of oocyte meiosis obviates this need, raising fundamental questions about the existence and necessity of Golgi disassembly in oocytes. Herein, we demonstrated the existence of a Golgi disassembly process during oocyte meiosis I, which peaked at germinal vesicle breakdown (GVBD) and was largely completed by metaphase II (MII). item.description: PURPOSE OF REVIEW: To summarize current understanding of the epidemiology, pathogenesis and management of HIV-Associated Nephropathy (HIVAN) and other forms of Apolipoprotein L1 (APOL1)-mediated chronic kidney disease (CKD) in people of African ancestry with HIV.

item.title: Prednisolone attenuates the immunomodulatory capacity and reshapes the functional phenotype of canine adipose-derived mesenchymal stromal cells
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Prednisolone reshapes cADSC function in a context-dependent manner, reducing immunomodulatory capacity without substantially impairing viability. These findings suggest that glucocorticoid exposure and inflammatory activation interact to modulate cADSC function and should be considered when optimizing MSC-based therapy for canine CIE.

item.title: Hope, hype, and high costs: Navigating glucagon-like Peptide-1 based therapy initiation among young adults
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Within this sample, GLP-1 initiation among young adults was shaped by intersecting health needs, social influences, access structures, and financial constraints rather than by clinical considerations alone. Findings highlight that healthcare systems, policymakers, and public health practitioners must prioritize clinically appropriate access, reliable medication sourcing, and consistent clinical oversight to promote equity and safety among young adults.

item.title: Clinical practice guideline for renal replacement therapy in critically ill patients with acute kidney injury (2026 edition)
item.description: Acute kidney injury (AKI) is a common and severe complication in critically ill patients, associated with high morbidity and mortality. Renal replacement therapy (RRT) is a vital life-support modality for critically ill patients with AKI. However, there remains a lack of unified clinical standards for core issues including the timing of RRT initiation, treatment modality, anticoagulation strategy, and weaning from RRT. In response, the Chinese Society of Critical Care Medicine organized a...

item.title: Antifungal activity of propolis against Candida spp
item.description: Fungal infections caused by Candida species remain a major clinical and pharmacological challenge, ranging from superficial mucocutaneous disease to invasive infections associated with considerable morbidity. Vulvovaginal candidiasis is among the most common manifestations and is frequently recurrent. Increasing antifungal resistance has reduced the effectiveness of azoles and other standard therapies, highlighting the need for alternative or complementary treatment strategies. This systematic...

item.title: Implementation of Provider-Facing Interventions to Increase Uptake of Endoscopic Screening for Esophageal Adenocarcinoma
item.description: CONCLUSION: Both provider notifications and nurse outreach demonstrated high acceptability and completion but limited feasibility for increasing EGD orders due to provider and system-level barriers, highlighting implementation gaps and targets for guideline and workflow integration.

item.description: CONCLUSIONS: No statistically significant differences in neonatal pain ratings or pupillary responses were detected following routine night-shift work, whereas exploratory eye-tracking measures suggested differences in visual-attentional patterns. Given the small, selected sample and exploratory design, these findings do not establish equivalent or preserved performance between conditions. item.title: Closing the hospice gap: the value of home-based medical care
item.description: CONCLUSION: As more older adults age in the community and hospice services expand to support patients with complex illnesses such as dementia, HBMC may offer a valuable strategy for effectively navigating prognosis uncertainty and the complexities of hospice eligibility requirements and enrollment.

item.title: Effect of Virtual Reality Relaxation on Alarm Fatigue and Professional Quality of Life Among Nurses in Intensive Care Units
item.description: CONCLUSION: The significant improvement in AFS and ProQOL scores indicates that the use of new technologies, such as virtual reality can be considered as a complementary tool in promoting the mental and professional health of nurses in stressful environments.

item.title: Predictive Value of the Systemic Immune-Inflammation Index for Cardiovascular Events in Patients With Chronic Total Coronary Occlusion
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Baseline SII is a reliable and independent predictor of MACEs in patients with CTO after PCI, with superior predictive performance compared with conventional inflammatory markers.

item.title: Skirted Prosthetic Valves Are Associated With Increased Risk of Subclinical Leaflet Thrombosis Following Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement: A Multicenter Study
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Over one-quarter of patients undergoing TAVR using SEVs developed SLT within six months. The use of skirted prosthetic valves was independently associated with SLT.

item.description: Oral ulcers are complex mucosal lesions characterized by infection, inflammatory imbalance, elevated oxidative stress and impaired vascular regeneration, with therapeutic efficacy hindered by rapid drug loss in the highly wet and dynamic oral environment. Here, we developed a Janus-structured bacterial cellulose (BC)-based multifunctional oral patch (Ber@ZIF/BC, BZB) for stable retention and controlled release of Ber@ZIF (BZ) at ulcer sites. item.title: Longitudinal Integrated Clerkship versus Traditional Rotation-Based Clerkships: A Class-Wide Comparison
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: The LIC model can be used for an entire cohort of medical students. This is evidenced by no statistically significant difference in USMLE Step 2 scores and NBME subject examination scores, except for three clerkships where LIC students scored higher. OSCE scores indicate that schools will need to ensure LIC students have opportunities to further develop their clinical skills and note writing.

item.description: Commercial food packaging materials are mainly synthesized from non-renewable petroleum-based polymers. Starch-based bioplastics have been developed as an alternative material since they are renewable and environmentally friendly. item.title: A Single-Center Retrospective Analysis of the Diagnostic Efficacy of Transthoracic Echocardiography in the Classification of Patent Ductus Arteriosus
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Among true-positive cases, TTE has high sensitivity for diagnosing tubular PDA and high specificity for diagnosing funnel-type PDA. Meanwhile, TTE shows good agreement with DSA in measuring key parameters. Furthermore, TTE demonstrates stability in the diagnostic classification of PDA, with no significant influence from operator variability. TTE could serve as a reliable basis for clinical decision-making to aid in the diagnostic classification of PDA.

item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Partial upper sternotomy for extensive arch repair was feasible and was not associated with an apparent increase in perioperative adverse events. Compared with full sternotomy, PUS was associated with less reported pain, lower psychological burden, and better early postoperative HRQoL in selected patients with AAAD.

item.description: Universal access to safe drinking water is called for under Sustainable Development Target 6.1 (SDG 6.1). Yet quantitative evidence on disease reductions associated with achieving SDG 6.1 and the service dimensions that most effectively reduce diarrhoeal diseases remains limited and inconsistent. item.description: Topological textures of light offer powerful routes to structure optical fields, control wave transport, and manipulate matter. item.description: Cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) syndrome represents a complex interplay among cardiovascular disease, chronic kidney disease, and metabolic disorders; meanwhile, CKM syndrome affects a significant proportion of adults and increases the risk of heart failure, end-stage renal disease, and premature death. item.description: Bacillus species, which are among the most extensively studied and widely used rhizobacteria, have demonstrated potent antagonistic activity against a broad spectrum of phytopathogenic fungi, making them ideal microorganisms for biological control. item.description: Missing data are ubiquitous in biomedical research, and become particularly problematic when combining data from multiple clinical studies, an increasingly common practice for building models that generalise across populations. item.description: The treatment of borderline hip dysplasia (BHD) remains controversial, with a paucity of literature on whether periacetabular osteotomy (PAO) is a viable option even in middle-aged patients over 30 years of age. This study aimed to analyse the functional outcome and activity level in relation to the patient's age after PAO for BHD. item.description: From clinical and ethical perspectives, the need for scientific evidence establishing safety and efficacy of high-risk therapeutic medical devices, and for transparency of that evidence, is similar to new drugs-but requirements for devices and drugs have developed quite differently. item.description: Since its development, the Fear of Missing Out (FoMO) scale has been widely used to measure addictive behaviour towards information and communication technologies. However, its French adaptation and associated psychometric properties have not been validated. This study aimed at addressing this gap in the literature and proposed a validated measure for French-speaking populations. item.description: Cannabis use in adolescence has been linked to lower adult cognitive function, but the specific contributions of age of onset and usage frequency remain unclear. This study analyzed data from the Zurich Project on Social Development from Childhood to Adulthood (z-proso; N = 1522) to examine associations between adolescent cannabis use and cognitive performance at young adulthood. item.description: Human induced pluripotent stem cell (hiPSC)-derived liver organoids have emerged as valuable models for studying human liver development. item.title: In situ synthesized free-standing LiCoPO4@C nanofibers with multifunctional electrochemical activity for lithium-ion and lithium-sulfur batteries
item.description: Free-standing LiCoPO(4)@C (LCP@C) nanofibers were synthesized by one-pot electrospinning of precursor salts followed by controlled pre-oxidation and carbonization at 400-460 °C. Pre-oxidation temperature controlled a trade-off between crystallinity and carbon retention: moderate treatment (440 °C) yielded uniformly dispersed nanoparticles within a continuous carbon fiber network, while lower and higher temperatures led to compositional heterogeneity and severe carbon depletion, respectively....

item.title: rAAV-mediated multi-miRNA delivery targeting MAPK pathway suppresses laser-induced choroidal neovascularization in mice
item.description: Age-related macular degeneration (AMD) is a leading cause of irreversible vision loss, with neovascular AMD (nAMD) characterized by choroidal neovascularization (CNV) and subretinal fibrosis. Although anti-VEGF therapy is the current standard, frequent injections and limited efficacy necessitate alternative treatments. The mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK) pathway contributes to AMD by promoting oxidative stress-induced apoptosis, inflammation, and angiogenesis. We evaluated the...

item.title: Coordinated epigenomic reprogramming and chromatin-mediated transcriptional regulation during soybean callus development
item.description: INTRODUCTION: Callus formation is a fundamental developmental process involving cellular dedifferentiation and regeneration in plants. However, the epigenetic mechanisms underlying this process remain poorly understood.

item.title: Age-Specific Changes in Chewing Discomfort During the Expansion of National Health Insurance Coverage for Dental Implants: A Controlled Interrupted Time Series Analysis in South Korea, 2010-2024
item.description: CONCLUSION: These findings indicate substantial secular improvement and age-specific heterogeneity in policy-timed changes in chewing discomfort, with the most consistent additional decline observed among adults aged 70-74 years. However, they do not establish an implant-specific treatment effect and highlight the need for age-sensitive, post-implementation evaluation and refinement of dental coverage based on functional outcomes.

item.title: Early BMP7 Exposure Enhances Brown Adipogenic Differentiation of Tonsil-Derived Mesenchymal Stem Cells
item.description: CONCLUSION: This early commitment modulation study demonstrates that temporal BMP7 exposure enhances brown adipocyte-like features and adrenergic sensitivity in TMSCs. Early stage-specific signaling modulation provides a viable strategy for directing stem cell lineage commitment toward brown adipocyte-like phenotypes for metabolic research.

item.title: Anti-inflammatory effects of JI-017 in cellular and an LPS-induced endotoxemia model
item.description: CONCLUSION: Under the experimental conditions examined, JI-017 reduced inflammatory responses and was associated with improved survival in an acute LPS-induced endotoxemia model. These findings support further preclinical investigation of JI-017.

item.title: Quality of Life Trajectories After Partial Laryngectomy Versus Total Laryngectomy Stratified by Voice Rehabilitation Success
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Voice rehabilitation status may be associated with long-term QoL patterns after laryngeal cancer surgery. Successful rehabilitation after TL may be associated with more favorable long-term QoL patterns, with outcomes in selected domains approaching those of the PL group, whereas unsuccessful rehabilitation may be associated with persistently poorer outcomes.

item.title: Corrigendum to "CATA-optimize-to-ideal (CATA-OI): A consumer-driven product optimization method compared with liking/disliking CATA and ideal profile method" [Food Res. Int. 243 (2026) 120344]
item.description: No abstract

item.title: Mist spraying vs. immersion of riboflavin for blue light-mediated photodynamic inactivation of Escherichia coli O157:H7
item.description: This study compared the antimicrobial efficacy and food quality effects of riboflavin combined with 405 nm blue light (RB + BL) applied via mist and immersion approaches against E. coli O157:H7 on stainless steel (SUS) surfaces and sliced ham. On bacteria-inoculated SUS surfaces, the mist RB + BL treatment achieved 4.39 log CFU/cm² reduction at 20 J/cm² and reduced microbial counts to below the detection limit at 40 J/cm², whereas the immersion RB + BL treatment reached only 3.45 log CFU/cm²...

item.title: PRAP1 aggravates palmitate-induced insulin resistance in skeletal muscle cells through a CD36-dependent mechanism
item.description: Proline-rich acidic protein 1 (PRAP1) is involved in intestinal lipid handling, but its role in skeletal muscle insulin resistance is unknown. We examined circulating PRAP1 in normal diet- and high-fat diet-fed mice and evaluated PRAP1 expression and secretion in palmitate-treated intestinal epithelial cells, together with its functional effects in differentiated C2C12 myotubes. PRAP1 expression and secretion were assessed following palmitate exposure, while C2C12 myotubes were treated with...

item.title: Comparison of signal drop on T2-weighted and post-contrast T1-weighted Dixon MRI in spinal bone marrow lesions
item.description: CONCLUSION: GdT1 %drop was significantly lower than T2 %drop with substantially lower specificity, warranting cautious interpretation to avoid misclassification.

item.title: Cleavage-gated Cas13-to-DNA nanostructure transduction for target-preamplification-free viral RNA detection
item.description: CRISPR-Cas13a enables programmable RNA recognition without target nucleic-acid preamplification, but conventional assays encode collateral RNase activity by cleaving fluorescent reporters. Here, we developed a cleavage-gated strategy that converts transient Cas13a cleavage into a sequence-defined, strand-displacement-competent DNA actuator, shifting signal encoding from cumulative reporter intensity to a discrete scaffold topology. A chimeric masking hairpin (CMH) links Cas13a to a DNA...

item.title: Harnessing molecular symmetry for metalloprotein design
item.description: Metalloprotein design has progressed from minimalist strategies that recapitulate only primary coordination spheres to approaches that construct secondary coordination spheres or nonbiological metallocofactors within entirely new metalloprotein scaffolds. In numerous natural systems, active sites often exhibit intrinsic pseudosymmetry or are located at protein-protein interfaces within symmetric assemblies. Inspired by these features, metalloprotein design efforts leverage the inherent molecular...

item.title: Factors Influencing the Treatment Response of Tetracyclines for Papulopustular Rash Induced by Epidermal Growth Factor Receptor-Tyrosine Kinase Inhibitors: A Retrospective Study
item.description: No abstract

item.title: Factors associated with premenstrual syndrome and menstrual pain in women of childbearing age
item.description: BackgroundThis study investigated variables associated with Premenstrual Syndrome (PMS) and Menstrual Pain in women of childbearing age to provide foundational data for improving quality of life.ObjectivesThis study aimed to examine variables associated with premenstrual syndrome and menstrual pain among women of childbearing age.DesignA cross-sectional descriptive survey design was used.MethodsA survey of 245 women of childbearing age in the metropolitan area was conducted using online...

item.title: Preoperative Thoracic Compensation is Associated With a Lower Risk of Proximal Junctional Kyphosis After Lower Thoracic Fusion for Adult Spinal Deformity
item.description: Study DesignRetrospective cohort study.ObjectivesTo determine whether thoracic compensation (TC) assessed against the deformity burden is associated with proximal junctional kyphosis (PJK) after lower thoracic fusion for adult spinal deformity (ASD).MethodsWe reviewed 343 patients fused from T9-L1 to the sacrum or pelvis with a pelvic incidence (PI) minus lumbar lordosis (LL) mismatch above 20°. Expected thoracic kyphosis (TK) was derived from the PI-LL mismatch using published equations, and a...

item.title: Cardiac Reverse Remodeling and Clinical Outcomes Following Angiotensin Receptor-Neprilysin Inhibitor Therapy in Heart Failure With Reduced Ejection Fraction
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Cardiac reverse remodeling after ARNI therapy varies among patients with HF with reduced EF. Positive responders to ARNI therapy at 1 year experienced more favorable clinical outcomes.

item.title: Total parenteral nutrition exposure in neonates and the risk of long-term food allergy: A retrospective cohort study
item.description: CONCLUSION: Neonatal TPN exposure was not significantly associated with the long-term risk of food allergy. The unadjusted association appears attributable to confounding by baseline clinical severity, although a modest increase in risk cannot be excluded.

item.title: Gut microbiome shifts during frog development parallel host-association patterns across vertebrate lineages
item.description: The developmental habitat transitions between aquatic and terrestrial environments in frogs offer a compelling model to investigate how environmental shifts shape gut microbiota. However, our understanding of how these transitions influence gut microbial communities across frog development remains limited. Here, we investigated how habitat changes during frog development affect gut microbiota composition and compared these patterns with host-microbiome interactions across vertebrates. Frog gut...

item.title: No easy fix for adherence in internet interventions: two randomized studies targeting adherence self-efficacy
item.description: Low adherence remains a persistent challenge in self-guided internet interventions, and universal strategies are needed to address it. In this study, we designed and evaluated a brief self-guided add-on module aimed at strengthening self-efficacy specific to adhering to internet interventions. The module included a testimonial video and two text-based exercises grounded in self-efficacy theory. It targeted self-efficacy specific to integrating and maintaining use of internet interventions. In...

item.title: Mental Health Challenges and Workplace Risk Factors Among Sexual and Gender Minority Workers in Korea
item.description: CONCLUSION: SGM workers face disproportionate mental health challenges related to adverse working conditions and discrimination, highlighting the need for targeted protective strategies.

item.title: Effects of Evogliptin and Dapagliflozin on Bone and Glucose Metabolism in Postmenopausal Women with Type 2 Diabetes: A Multicenter Randomized Exploratory Clinical Trial
item.description: CONCLUSION: In postmenopausal women with T2DM, BMD remained stable with evogliptin, whereas dapagliflozin was associated with a small reduction in femoral neck BMD, although this finding was weakened after adjustment. These findings provide preliminary evidence regarding the skeletal effects of evogliptin and dapagliflozin and warrant confirmation in larger studies.

item.title: Redefining Worker Protection in the Algorithmic Era: From Algorithmic Justice to Insurance Systems for the Gig Economy
item.description: The rapid expansion of the digital platform economy has introduced novel occupational hazards driven by algorithmic management. This short communication examines the occupational health challenges faced by gig workers in the context of algorithmic control, focusing on four key mechanisms: trade-offs between economic success and worker health, uncertainty in terms of effort and reward, unreliable assessment of job performance, and incorrect attribution of responsibility. These algorithmic hazards...

item.title: Upward changes in serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D levels in South Korea: the Korea National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey studies IX (2022-2023) versus VI (2013-2014)
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Over the past decade, South Korea has experienced an upward shift in population-level vitamin D concentrations. These changes may be associated with increased intake of dietary supplements, but because direct standardization of analytical methods has not been achieved, the relative contributions of behavioral changes and analytical method-related differences cannot be quantified.

item.title: Physical Activity and Cognitive Function in Postmenpausal Women: Depressive Symptoms and Sleep Disorder as Sequential Mediators
item.description: CONCLUSION: In postmenopausal women, moderate PA is associated with better cognitive function, partly through fewer depressive symptoms and improved sleep, whereas high-intensity physical labor is associated with poorer cognition. Depressive symptoms and sleep may therefore be relevant considerations when planning strategies to preserve cognitive health in this population.

item.title: An evidence-informed occupational health curriculum for pre-deployment preparation of aquanauts in underwater habitats: a scenario-based framework development study
item.description: CONCLUSION: This article offers a preliminary occupational health curriculum for pre-deployment preparation that underwater habitat programs can adapt. It is evidence-informed and unvalidated. The framework addresses worker protection within a bounded underwater workplace while preserving the authority of diving, clinical, and mission-governance systems. Independent stakeholder review, instructor usability testing, pilot training, and analog-mission observation remain necessary before the...

item.title: Direction-dependent biomechanical effects of transverse process hooks versus pedicle screws at the uppermost instrumented vertebra in adult spinal deformity: a finite element analysis
item.description: Proximal junctional complications are often driven by abrupt mechanical transition at the uppermost instrumented vertebra (UIV). This study used patient-specific finite element analysis to compare biomechanical effects of transverse process hooks and pedicle screws at the UIV, specifically examining how hook orientation influences anterior-posterior load sharing. A validated nonlinear three-dimensional T7-L2 spinal model was developed using data from a 60-year-old woman. Three UIV constructs...

item.title: Case Report: Computed tomographic diagnosis of asymmetric bilateral uterine horn torsion secondary to benign uterine leiomyomas in a non-gravid dog
item.description: Uterine torsion is uncommon in dogs and most commonly involves a single uterine horn. An 11-year-old intact female Pomeranian was presented with a 2- to 3-day history of abdominal distension, dyspnea, anorexia, vomiting, and oliguria. Clinicopathologic findings indicated renal compromise, electrolyte abnormalities, tissue injury, and marked systemic inflammation. Radiography and ultrasonography revealed large bilateral abdominal masses with peritoneal effusion, although the organ of origin could...

item.title: Deep learning prediction of MSI/dMMR, EBV, HER2, PD-L1, and CLDN18.2 status directly from hematoxylin and eosin-stained slides in gastric and gastroesophageal junction adenocarcinoma: a systematic review
item.description: CONCLUSION: Individual held-out models sometimes showed promising discrimination, particularly for EBV and MSI/dMMR, but the evidence was too sparse, dependent, and heterogeneous to define a stable summary performance or a clinically deployable triage threshold. Certainty was very low for MSI/dMMR, EBV, HER2, and PD-L1 and low for CLDN18.2; clinical utility and calibrated threshold performance remain unestablished.

item.title: What students pursue matters: longitudinal associations between goal contents and life skills in university physical education
item.description: INTRODUCTION: Research on goal contents has largely focused on why students engage in physical activity, with less attention to what they pursue through it. This study examined the prospective and possible reverse-direction associations between intrinsic and extrinsic goal contents and five life skills among students in university physical education.

item.title: Correction: Unlocking the potential of immunotherapy for patients with resectable non-small cell lung cancer
item.description: [This corrects the article DOI: 10.3389/fonc.2025.1690367.].

item.title: Impact of the Serious Accidents Punishment Act on Occupational Injury Rates in Korea's Manufacturing Sector: An Interrupted Time-Series Analysis
item.description: CONCLUSION: SAPA implementation was not associated with statistically significant changes in injury rates in most subgroups after multiple testing adjustment, consistent with the early post-implementation experience of analogous international legislation. Exploratory subgroup analyses suggested differential responses by sex and company size, necessitating longitudinal research to evaluate the law's long-term preventive effects.

item.title: Triglyceride-glucose index and preserved ratio impaired spirometry in 89,809 individuals without self-reported overt clinical disease
item.description: INTRODUCTION: While both preserved ratio impaired spirometry (PRISm) and triglyceride glucose index (TyG) are established risk factors for cardiometabolic diseases, the metabolic characteristics and prevalence of PRISm differ by ethnic group. However, this association has not been directly examined in Asian populations. Therefore, we aimed to investigate whether TyG is associated with PRISm in a large Korean population without self-reported overt clinical disease.

item.title: Landscape of cancer genomics and precision oncology in Japan, South Korea, China, and Australia
item.description: Precision oncology has expanded rapidly across the Asia-Pacific region, yet implementation remains heterogeneous because of differences in health-system organisation, reimbursement, molecular tumour board infrastructure, workforce capacity, and data integration. This structured narrative review with expert consultation compares precision oncology ecosystems in Japan, South Korea, China, and Australia to identify common challenges and implementation strategies across the patient pathway. Although...

item.title: Nationwide Outcomes and Predictors of Mortality After Left Ventricular Assist Device Implantation in Korea: Insights From the Korean Registry for Mechanically Assisted Circulatory Support
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: In this high-acuity population with frequent preoperative ECMO support, nationwide LVAD outcomes were comparable to international benchmarks. Mortality was more closely associated with preoperative clinical status than with treatment strategy.

item.title: P-CAB - amoxicillin dual therapy for H. pylori eradication: a narrative review of efficacy, safety, and guideline positioning
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: P-CAB-amoxicillin dual therapy is a promising, antibiotic-sparing candidate for H. pylori eradication, with efficacy comparable to BQT and a potentially lower adverse-event burden. Comparative evidence against concomitant therapy remains limited. Dedicated regional RCTs are needed before incorporation into national guidelines.

item.title: Perceived headache responses to exercise in patients with migraine: A cross-sectional study
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Perceived headache responses to exercise are highly heterogeneous and vary according to migraine burden and clinical characteristics. These findings underscore the importance of individualized clinical counseling over uniform exercise recommendations in migraine management.

item.title: Multi-class Identification and Quantification of Breast Implant-related Complications in Ultrasonography Using a Pathology-informed Lesion Graph: A Deep Learning Development and Validation Study
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: The proposed multiscale model delivers a comprehensive, clinical-grade output, comprising accurate complication classification, five-zone spatial localization, and objective morphometric metrics, while mitigating operator dependency. This system holds strong potential as an accessible, high-performance decision support tool for long-term safety screening of patients with breast implants.

item.title: Albuminuria and hematologic profiles across eGFR categories in U.S. adults: NHANES 2001-2018 with detailed iron-biomarker analysis
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: The prespecified mean-hemoglobin hypothesis was not supported. Higher UACR was associated with threshold-defined anemia as a secondary outcome, while small red-cell and iron-marker differences did not establish conventional absolute iron deficiency or imply changes in anemia management.

item.title: A case of recurrent early gastric cancer with a giant injection-related granuloma after endoscopic submucosal dissection resulting in non-curative resection
item.description: A 69-year-old man underwent endoscopic submucosal dissection (ESD) for early gastric cancer of the lower gastric body. The lateral margin was positive, corresponding to an eCura C-1 classification, and surveillance with upper gastrointestinal endoscopy every 6 months was performed. Local recurrence was detected 4 years later, and repeat ESD resulted in an eCura C-2 classification, prompting additional surgical resection. No lymph node metastasis was identified, and the patient remained...

item.title: Yawning in lungfishes: occurrence and potential functional differences between respiratory modes
item.description: Yawning is a stereotyped behavioural pattern observed across vertebrates and is considered multifunctional, but how its function changed during major physiological transitions remains poorly understood. Lungfishes provide an ideal model to address this question because species vary in their relative reliance on branchial and pulmonary respiration. We investigated whether yawning occurs in one individual each of the branchial-dominant Australian lungfish and three pulmonary-dominant species...

item.title: Non-invasive diagnosis of invasive aspergillosis in patients with haematological malignancies: a prospective diagnostic accuracy study
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: uTafC/Cr or sGM provides an Aspergillus-focused non-invasive adjunct to BALF-based testing; sPtx3 increased case detection but had limited specificity and requires prospective validation.

item.title: Altered stimulus-intensity encoding occurs in the primary somatosensory cortex of a central post-stroke pain rat model
item.description: Central post-stroke pain (CPSP) is a chronic form of pain that develops after ventral posterolateral thalamus (VPL) lesions and may involve maladaptive plasticity within central somatosensory pathways. Although abnormalities in the primary somatosensory cortex (S1) are observed in patients and animal models, the mechanism by which thalamic lesions alter cortical processing of sensory stimuli remains unclear. Here, we investigated stimulus intensity encoding and dendritic remodeling in S1 using a...

item.title: 50 years of Ebola research and response
item.description: No abstract

item.title: Facilitating bi-directional extracellular electron transfer via the n-type conducting polymer poly(benzodifurandione)
item.description: Shewanella oneidensis MR-1 is a model electroactive bacterium capable of bidirectional extracellular electron transfer (EET), though inward EET remains energetically challenging due to the low potential required for intracellular reduction. Here, we report the use of poly(benzodifurandione) (PBFDO), an n-type conducting polymer, as an electrode modifier to enhance both outward and inward EET in S. oneidensis MR-1. The PBFDO-modified electrode exhibited improved biofilm morphology and cell...

item.title: Interactions between vaginal, periurethral and urinary microbiota in genitourinary syndrome of menopause and the effects of local estrogen therapy
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Microbial alterations in genitourinary syndrome of menopause are compartment-specific and extend beyond the vagina. Periurethral microbiota may contribute to symptom expression, while local estrogen therapy promotes restoration of Lactobacillus-dominant urogenital microbiota.

item.title: Application of generalized perturbation theory to hill climbing-based optimization of material arrangement in beam shaping assembly for BNCT
item.description: In order to realize broad-range search in optimization problems of material selection and their arrangement in the design of Beam Shaping Assembly (BSA), a new method combining the generalized perturbation theory (GPT) to the hill climbing algorithm is proposed. In this method, all possible candidate solutions neighboring a current solution are thoroughly considered, and difference of each of these candidates from the current one in the objective function and the constraints is rapidly estimated...

item.title: Toxicological profiles in adolescent suicide before and after COVID-19: A forensic autopsy study of the involvement of over-the-counter medications and sex differences in urban Japan
item.description: Adolescent suicide remains a major public health concern, with recent increases observed, particularly among females in Japan. However, the toxicological characteristics in forensic settings have not yet been sufficiently described. This study examined the toxicological patterns in adolescent suicide cases before and after the onset of the coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) pandemic, using forensic autopsy data from three institutions in metropolitan Japan (2015-2024). A total of 41 cases (10...

item.title: Feedback-controlled single-frequency microwave thermal cycling enables dynamic modulation of liposome membrane permeability
item.description: Liposomes are widely used as delivery platforms for therapeutic drugs, nucleic acids, and diagnostic agents. Because cargo release is governed by the permeability of the lipid bilayer, controlling membrane permeability is essential for regulating molecular release from liposomes. Various stimuli, including pH, light, ultrasound, magnetic fields, and temperature, have been explored to control liposomal membrane permeability and cargo release. Among these approaches, microwave (MW) irradiation has...

item.title: Transformations in nursing education: Voices of senior faculty members with decades of experience
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Senior nursing faculty members in Türkiye are navigating interlocking structural pressures that have destabilized the professional foundations of nursing academia. Urgent institutional responses are needed, including restructuring academic roles to protect clinical engagement, supporting pedagogical adaptation, and reconceptualizing promotion criteria to honor the full breadth of nursing scholarly contribution.

item.title: Oral texture perception: Behavioral evidence and neural mechanisms
item.description: CONCLUSION: Behavioral paradigms that minimize chemical cues demonstrate that rats can use the physical properties of food as oral sensory cues. These models provide a foundation for identifying the receptors and neural circuits underlying oral texture perception, and for understanding how texture information is integrated with taste.

item.title: Dermoscopy-Based AI Risk Scoring Enhanced Experienced Dermatologists' Decision-Making: a Large Retrospective Reader Study
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: AI enhanced experienced dermatologists' decision-making, particularly for melanoma and high-grade dysplastic naevi. Future prospective studies should further explore AI's integration into routine clinical settings.

item.title: Autocrine feedback maintains homeostatic neuropeptide expression in a peptidergic hub neuron
item.description: Neuronal circuits sustain stable function by self-regulating their gene expression and neurosecretion. Patterns for autocrine feedback by neuropeptides are widespread across nervous systems, but how they contribute to neuronal homeostasis is less well understood. Here, we identify an autocrine homeostatic mechanism in a C. elegans peptidergic hub neuron. FLP-1 neuropeptide release activates the inhibitory receptor DMSR-7 on the AVK hub neurons to self-regulate flp-1 transcription, dense-core...

item.title: Surgery and/or biologics in chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyps: EUFOREA/EPOS consensus paper
item.description: The therapeutic landscape of chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyps (CRSwNP) has rapidly evolved over the past 6 years with the arrival of biologics, prompting a re-evaluation of the traditional stepwise management centred on corticosteroids and endoscopic sinus surgery (ESS). Although both ESS and biologics have proven efficacy, the optimal sequence, extent and timing of ESS relative to biologics remains a matter of debate. The international multidisciplinary panel of experts of EUFOREA/EPOS...

item.title: New CRS control tests: development and validation by EUFOREA
item.description: CONCLUSION: The brief CCT and the longer CPCT are new CRS control tests that show moderate to high correlations with existing tools. Both instruments demonstrated good psychometric properties and therefore can be recommended for use in clinical practice and research.

item.title: Three-dimensional Motion Capture Discriminates Extremely Mild Cerebellar Ataxia from Parkinsonism in the Upper Limbs
item.description: Upper-limb motor symptoms in spinocerebellar degeneration (SCD) and Parkinson's disease (PD) frequently overlap, making clinical differentiation challenging in mild cases using the finger-to-nose test (FNT) or the diadochokinesis test (DDKT). This study aimed to identify quantitative kinematic markers that distinguish mild SCD from mild PD using three-dimensional motion capture. Twenty-six individuals per group-mild SCD, mild PD, and normal controls (NCs)--underwent motion analysis during FNT...

item.title: A Case of Fetal-Type Posterior Communicating Artery Aneurysm Suffered from Thromboembolic and Perforator Occlusion after Flow Diverter Therapy
item.description: Flow diverter placement for fetal-type posterior communicating artery (PCom) aneurysms is known to result in a low complete occlusion rate due to the tendency for flow out toward the PCom, resulting in residual blood flow within the aneurysm. Here, we report a case of ischemic complications after flow diverter treatment for a fetal-type PCom bifurcation aneurysm. Seventy-five-year-old woman had unruptured left fetal-type PCom. Pipeline placement with coils was performed. Eight months after...

item.title: Staged Bilateral Microvascular Decompression for Bilateral Hemifacial Spasm
item.description: Bilateral hemifacial spasm (BHFS) is rare and typically arises from neurovascular compression of the facial nerve. Optimal treatment strategies, including the timing and laterality of microvascular decompression (MVD), remain uncertain. We report a case of a 43-year-old man with a 10-year history of left hemifacial spasm, and right-sided symptoms beginning 1 year prior to initial evaluation. Magnetic resonance imaging demonstrated bilateral neurovascular compression at the root exit zone. The...

item.title: Peripheral transition metalation: hemilabile meso-N-metalated phthalocyanines showing activatable near-infrared photophysical properties
item.description: Phthalocyanine is one of the most important organic functional dyes in materials and life sciences, due to its intense absorption and emission in the red-to-near-IR (NIR) regions. Various transition metal elements can be included in the phthalocyanine core through coordination of the pyrrolic nitrogen atoms, resulting in characteristic properties, but the bridging meso-nitrogen atoms have not yet been utilized as ligands for transition metals. We hypothesized that weak, reversible...

item.title: Early-Phase Computed Tomography Bowel Diameter and Neurological Outcomes Post-Extracorporeal Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation
item.description: CONCLUSION: The results of this exploratory investigation suggest that bowel diameter may represent a potential adjunctive marker associated with functional outcomes post-ECPR for OHCA.

item.title: From pixels to prediction: improving imaging through AI in rheumatology
item.description: Imaging plays a central role in the diagnosis, monitoring, and prediction of rheumatic and musculoskeletal diseases (RMDs), yet its clinical and regulatory impact remains limited by variability, the lack of standardisation and metrics for quantification, and slow clinical translation. Artificial intelligence (AI) offers unique opportunities to overcome these barriers through automated segmentation, quantitative feature extraction, and multimodal data integration. The AutoPiX consortium seeks to...

item.title: Bobble-Head Doll Syndrome Caused by Aqueductal Web-Associated Obstructive Hydrocephalus in an Adult: A Case Report with Video
item.description: BACKGROUND: Bobble-head doll syndrome (BHDS) is a rare movement disorder usually observed in children and associated with third ventricular lesions or hydrocephalus.

item.title: Electrolyzed saline coolant mitigates bacterial airborne deposition in dental procedures
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: EOS demonstrated rapid contact-bactericidal activity and comparable dental spray deposition reduction to CHX. As a reasonably biocompatible, broad-spectrum agent, EOS may represent a promising coolant candidate for infection prevention control, warranting further clinical evaluation.

item.title: Sequential construction of Ru/B-regulated crystalline-amorphous interfaces in MOF-derived NiCo-LDH enables highly efficient bifunctional electrocatalysis
item.description: Although Metal-Organic Framework (MOF)-derived NiCo layered double hydroxides (LDHs) provide ideal hierarchical architectures for multifunctional interface engineering, rationally integrating such interfaces to cooperatively regulate the electronic structure and kinetics of both the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) and oxygen evolution reaction (OER) remains a significant challenge in high current alkaline water electrolysis. Herein, B-Ru-NiCo-LDH nanosheet arrays featuring...

item.title: hTERT associates with Rab7A to enhance autophagy and rescue oxLDL induced endothelial dysfunction
item.description: CONCLUSION: This study highlights a novel additional role of extra telomeric hTERT in contributing to endothelial resilience against atherogenic stress by rescuing endothelial dysfunction via enhancing the expression of autophagy-related gene expression and enhancing autophagy dynamics by associating with Rab7A.

item.title: High-affinity ELR+ CXC chemokines display balanced G protein-, GRK- and β-arrestin-associated transducer engagement at the viral G protein-coupled receptor ORF74
item.description: Open reading frame 74 (ORF74) is the single G protein-coupled receptor (GPCR) encoded in the genome of Kaposi's sarcoma-associated herpesvirus (KSHV). Due to its high constitutive activity and broad chemokine binding profile, ORF74 contributes to KSHV-associated diseases through autocrine and paracrine mechanisms that promote cell proliferation, inflammation and angiogenesis. Previous studies showed that ELR+ CXC chemokines (i.e., CXCL1-3 and CXCL5-8), which contain a conserved Glu-Leu-Arg...

item.title: Reliability of Implant- vs. Bone-Based Postoperative Measurements After Anatomic Total Shoulder Arthroplasty Using CT Imaging
item.description: In anatomic total shoulder arthroplasty (aTSA) research, postoperative anatomical measurements are often referenced to the reamed glenoid bone surface because the glenoid component is not fully visible on CT. However, the reliability of measurements based directly on the implant (implant-based method) and their agreement with the commonly used bone-based method remain unclear. In this study, CT scans from 29 patients undergoing primary aTSA were used to calculate postoperative glenoid...

item.title: Curative-intent lung resection after recovery from fulminant immune checkpoint inhibitor-associated myocarditis during neoadjuvant therapy: a case report
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Fulminant ICI-associated myocarditis does not necessarily preclude subsequent curative-intent lung resection. In highly selected patients, surgery may remain feasible after objective cardiac recovery, multidisciplinary reassessment, and shared decision-making with the patient. This case suggests that the acute management of life-threatening cardiovascular irAEs should be undertaken at centers with continuous on-site cardiology support, multidisciplinary care, and access to emergency...

item.title: Formulation-Specific Safety Issues of HIV Pre-exposure Prophylaxis Drugs: A Disproportionality Analysis of the FAERS Database
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: PrEP agents display distinct, formulation-specific and reproducible safety patterns in FAERS. Comparator choice substantially influences the detection and interpretation of SDRs and can help distinguish reproducible formulation-related reporting patterns from findings that may be driven by the clinical and reporting context. These insights highlight priority areas for future research.

item.title: The Economic and Humanistic Burden of Phenylketonuria Among Patients and Their Caregivers: A Systematic Literature Review
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Findings underscore the substantial financial, time, and psychological burden of PKU, particularly in relation to dietary management.

item.title: Social Capital, Ecological Context, and Mental Health Among Medical and Health-Sciences University Students: A Multilevel Study Across 20 Chinese Cities
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Social capital - and its relational dimension in particular - university type, and regional economic development are each independently associated with probable mental disorder among university students. Multilevel social and structural contexts should be considered in designing mental health interventions in higher education.

item.title: Recent advances in antituberculosis drugs and therapeutics: from mechanistic breakthroughs to clinical translation
item.description: Tuberculosis (TB), caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis, reclaimed its status as the deadliest single-pathogen infectious disease globally in 2023, accounting for 10.8 million new cases and 1.25 million deaths in 2023. The escalating crisis of drug-resistant TB, suboptimal BCG vaccine efficacy in adults, and persistent treatment gaps for vulnerable populations collectively drive an urgent shift toward mechanism-driven, precision-oriented therapeutic strategies.This review presents a critically...

item.title: Thyme essential oil (Thymus vulgaris) modulates methane mitigation and rumen fermentation in vitro: a dose-response study
item.description: This study evaluated the effects of thyme (Thymus vulgaris) essential oil (EO), applied as a conventional bulk extract or a nanosized nanoemulsion at inclusion levels of 0, 15, 30, and 45 µL/g dry matter (DM), on in vitro ruminal gas production kinetics, methane and carbon dioxide emissions, nutrient degradability, and fermentation end-products. Gas chromatography-mass spectrometry identified thymol (33.15%), 1,3,8-p-menthatriene (22.65%), and γ-terpinene (12.8%) as the dominant volatile...

item.title: Growth and reproductive responses of goat bucks to range grazing and concentrate-based production systems
item.description: This study aimed to evaluate the effects of range grazing and three concentrate-based production systems on the growth, sexual behavior, scrotal circumference, and semen quality of breeding bucks. A total of 40 yearling bucks (10 bucks/treatment) were randomly allocated to range grazing (T1) and three different roughage-to-concentrate ratios: 60:40% (T2), 50:50% (T3), and 40:60% (T4) on a DM basis for a period of 90 days. item.title: Cardiovascular events in aging Japanese people with hemophilia: a 3-year interim analysis of the ADVANCE Japan cohort
item.description: As life expectancy increases in people with hemophilia (PWH), cardiovascular disease (CVD) has emerged as an important comorbidity. However, prospective data on CVD occurrence and its clinical management remain limited. We performed a prespecified 3-year interim analysis of ADVANCE Japan, an ongoing 10-year multicenter prospective cohort study of PWH aged ≥ 40 years, to describe CVD occurrence, clinical management, bleeding outcomes, and associated changes in hemostatic treatment. item.title: Distribution of Losses Among Horse Race Bettors: An Analysis of Account-Based Player Tracking Data
item.description: Previous research on gambling loss patterns has mainly relied on self-reported data, which has some inherent biases (e.g., low accuracy). While some studies are based on large samples of horse bettors, few have examined how losses are distributed among them. The aim of this exploratory study was to examine the concentration of losses among gamblers playing horse betting games. item.title: Chronic Headache: The Interplay of Muscle Tension, its Discrimination, and Body Awareness
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Patients with CH exhibit a site-specific deficit in muscle tension discrimination, accompanied by elevated resting pericranial muscle tension, reduced body awareness, and maladaptive cognitive coping strategies. The association between catastrophizing and impaired discrimination highlights the interplay between cognitive-affective factors and psychophysiological dysregulation in CH.
